videos.title: Humans are teaching AI how to do their jobs
videos.focus: Independent reporting on AI training, job redesign and competing views of worker displacement
videos.summary: 60 Minutes reports on workers who train AI using professional expertise, examples of lawyers using partner-like AI personas, and competing claims about augmentation and displacement. The companion report includes perspectives from trainers, a vendor, labor researcher Clara Shih and economist Daron Acemoglu. Its October 4 age is disclosed as an editorial advisory.
videos.why_it_matters: Leaders can compare vendor optimism with worker and economist concerns, then measure task displacement, training roles, entry-level access and human decision responsibility before describing AI adoption as simple augmentation.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed the complete official CBS companion report and its full-transcript link, then confirmed the exact 13:15 program; after preroll, the signed-out full-length player advanced from 4.47 to 12.53 seconds.

quality_review.editorial_relevance: Independent 60 Minutes reporting compares worker, vendor, lawyer, nonprofit and economist perspectives on AI training, augmentation and displacement.
quality_review.reader_value: Readers can turn the competing claims into a task-level workforce review instead of accepting one optimistic or catastrophic forecast.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected as same-edition recovery after the protected history gate rejected a reused PBS URL; this exact CBS program has complete reporting evidence and sustained signed-out playback.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: The independent news report presents multiple competing sources and sells no AI product or training service.
quality_review.editorial_value_basis: The complete report provides substantive multi-source evidence about workforce redesign, training markets and displacement that readers can translate into task-level adoption and accountability reviews.
transferable_takeaways: Measure exposed tasks separately from whole jobs.
Compare vendor claims with worker and labor evidence.
Preserve human judgment and entry-level development pathways.

videos.title: How algorithms manipulate you (and how to fight back)
videos.focus: Expert dialogue on algorithmic influence, opacity and practical civic responses
videos.summary: Jen Golbeck and Shalini Kantayya discuss how recommender systems shape attention and behavior, why optimization goals and data practices remain opaque, and what individuals, institutions and policymakers can do. The complete TED conversation is substantive analysis rather than a tutorial; its July release date is preserved as an age advisory.
videos.why_it_matters: The conversation helps readers distinguish personal mitigation from institutional accountability, ask what an algorithm optimizes, and identify where transparency, audit access or policy changes matter more than individual settings.
